steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Oh, you really came, Judge Lavinia!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You must be Segretario Rubio's daughter, yes?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Yeah! I thought my father was just joking around when he said you'd come babysit me!

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: My friends and I all adore you.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Compared to people like my father, you're like, the only clean person in the government.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Do you not get along well with your father?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Meh, so-so, I guess.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I still like him as a person, because he always makes time for me and plays with me a lot.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: But you know, I think people like him, who only care about protecting themselves and not rocking the boat, really should have bigger goals in life.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: His old work friends who started out on the same level as him are way up there now.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: It took him this long to land a half-decent job, and he doesn't want to do anything more with it.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: His old work friends?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Yeah, one of them was Carracci, Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici, who just died not too long ago.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It's a dangerous job.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I know... But, I saw him on TV every day, and wise guys from all the big famiglie treated him really well.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I dunno, I just think it doesn't make sense trying to be a politician if you can't make it to that level.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That might be true.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: So, that's why I was really surprised when my father suddenly decided to become the new Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I'm not sure what finally made things click for him... But if he did it sooner, my mother probably wouldn't have divorced him.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Divorced?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Yeah, she thought he was a good-for-nothing, so she left him a few years ago.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: But my mother has a temper, so I decided to stay with my father.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Oh, by the way, you know how he got appointed ministro, right? Can you tell me more about it?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Sorry, I actually don't know anything...

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Aww, okay then.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Anyway, you can sit anywhere you'd like.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I'm not going anywhere today, but I do want to listen to my father's inaugural speech.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: (Segretario Rubio... keeps his room tidier than I would've expected.)

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: You're surprised too, huh? He probably seems like he'd be a total slob, but he keeps things pretty organized.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Oh right, and he keeps a diary.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Yeah, lemme think... Right, he keeps it over here.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: He only writes in it when he feels like it. It's not an every day thing.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: After years of jotting stuff down, he's still got all these blank pages.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Does he not care if you snoop around his things?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: It's totally fine. He left it there because he doesn't mind people reading it.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I've flipped through it a few times, but it's all boring stuff. I'd call it like, chronicles of a middle-aged man? Boring, it drags on and on.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: You can take a look if you want.

a.text: March 5th
I ran into Carracci at a restaurant. We had a drink for the first time in a long while.
Reminiscing about old times, I couldn't help but to get teary-eyed.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Signor Rubio, this is where you'll be giving your speech.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Please leave me.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: But we've got orders to protect you.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Nobody could get in here, right?

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Right. Okay.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Hmph. Power, huh.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Now I'll barricade the door with the sofa... This is about as much as I can do.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Well, Carracci, I won't keep you waiting much longer. See you soon.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: How's it looking?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: The doctor says the strike just missed her heart by a few centimeters, so she didn't die instantly.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: But, she's still in really bad shape.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Where's Texas?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: She's been in a stupor ever since she got back yesterday.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: She just sits there motionless. Won't even respond when I ask if she wants to eat.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Just give her some time. Croissant and I will guard the hospital, so please take care of her.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: No need to worry about me. You two look after yourselves.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: *sigh*... So bored.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh right, I heard there was supposed to be some speech today?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Maybe I'll give it a listen.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Buongiorno, my dear friends and citizens.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I imagine most of you don't know much about me, and I can't blame you for that.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: After all, I came held very minor and unimportant role of Segretario di Sicurezza Alimentare before this.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: In fact, I believe that most of our dear citizens, apart from the late Ministro Carracci and the honorable Judge Lavinia, know very little about our government.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I do not know Judge Lavinia very well, but I do have somewhat of a history with the late Ministro Carracci.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I believe it would be appropriate to begin my speech with him, a figure everyone here should already be familiar with.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Carracci and I both joined L'Autorità Garante della Concorrenza e del Mercato around the same time.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: He was strong and energetic, taking care of the fieldwork while I handled the paperwork behind the scenes.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: He became known within the system for his bold words and actions, and he even dared to challenge prominent famiglie.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: To be perfectly honest, it seemed like the guy was indomitable. He was almost taken out a few times by dissatisfied famiglie, but managed to weather the storm or push through the situation.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But at the time, L'Autorità staff saw him as a pain, and nobody wanted to help him.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: So the job of reporting to him naturally fell to me, unpopular as I was.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And let me tell you, that job took a whole lot out of me.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But at the same time, it filled me with a sense of accomplishment.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Though I could never be as direct and straightforward as him, I could do what I wanted to do through him vicariously, and that was a reward in itself.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Throughout this process, the two of us became fairly well-acquainted.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Leon, you were working with Carracci for the last two years, and I know you thought highly of him.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Does this account match with what you knew of him?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He certainly was energetic.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He knew exactly how to deal with the famiglie, and that went beyond just being tactful. He knew how to help them under the table while also getting them to serve his interests.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: A lot of what he wanted to do would've been blocked by various famiglie, but in his hands, he always managed to get things done, step by step.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I can tell you learned a lot from him.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I just thought there were some similarities in the way I saw things and the way he operated.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The days when problems can be solved with fighting and killing are over, padre mio.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If the famiglie are going to survive, they have to adapt accordingly.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You still don't understand, Leon.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What do I not understand?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You've subconsciously lumped yourself in with Lavinia and Carracci.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But don't ever forget, you are not one of them.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: If you really knew, you wouldn't be standing here.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Unfortunately, you're out of time.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Padre?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Leon, if you get through this alive...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's what it is.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Even though he was a thorn in the side of many famiglie, his talents were evident to all.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And so, he rose through the ranks long before I did.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: In fact, I thought he wouldn't last long after his promotion.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I used to think that, because he was never in a place where too many different interests overlapped, he wouldn't face any serious attempts on his life.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: If he kept behaving the same way he always did as he rose through the ranks, sooner or later, he was bound to step on toes that he could not afford to step on.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I was wrong.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: I never knew my father could be such a talkative person.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: What do you think, Judge Lavinia?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Judge Lavinia?
Lavinia seems completely oblivious to the calls of Rubio's daughter.
She is engrossed in the words of the diary in her hands.

a.text: May 3rd
Just resolved a small case, but it touched me deeply.
There's a problem that everyone is unaware of. Or, should I say, is turning a blind eye to.
Why, even in the age of Signora Sicilia, does Siracusa have two different sets of rules at once—one internal, and one external?
The brutality and greed of the famiglie have long been documented, but as brutal and greedy as they may be, they have chosen not to control things themselves.
There's a reason for this.
It's actually quite simple.
Population.
The institution of a famiglia is based on bloodline or personal identity.
And this inefficient organization means that the numbers in any given famiglia will never reach the order of magnitude required to manage even a nomadic city.
This means they must rely on a system established by the common citizenry, and they can only seize control of a behemoth such as Siracusa by manipulating this system behind the scenes.
Signora Sicilia was acutely aware of this fact, so after she rose to power, she drew an even more pronounced line between mafiosi and ordinary folk.

And by emphasizing her absolute might and control, she, over the past few decades, has gotten everyone in Siracusa to believe that in Siracusa, 'the existence of two orders, internal and external, is taken for granted.'
To the extent that everyone was forced to forget how the establishment of Siracusa's underground order was only made possible by the consistency of the outward-facing order.
This cannot be called anything other than a manifestation of political wisdom.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Rubio, you...

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: In fact, in our system, there is no shortage of people with the same fundamental intentions as Carracci.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: However, for various reasons, they finally chose to submit to these famiglie, even becoming their cronies.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But Carracci was different. Not only did he not give in, he was always looking for ways to fight against them.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And, his efforts paid off.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: He did not die as easily as I thought he would, and he even managed to climb higher.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And when we met again at a banquet, he said something that I will never forget—

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: 'The famiglie these days are weak.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: This dude's pretty brave...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Umm... Texas, there seems to be something happening outside. Lemme go check it out.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Exusiai.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Do you think... we could bring Giovanna back to Lungmen?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: She seems fun.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But, it doesn't feel like that's what you think. Right?
Texas turns her eyes to the table by the window, upon which a necklace sits.
It was a symbol of trust from Signora Sicilia.
A gift that Giovanna left for her.
In her grandfather's eyes, the Columbian famiglie had soured.
They'd do anything for the sake of profit, getting involved in the lowest businesses, committing murders with no morals at all.
In her father's eyes, the Siracusan famiglie had decayed.
Passing up profit and opportunity, not fighting for their interests, limiting their progress for the sake of supposed morality. All of it was the pinnacle of stupidity.
In Texas's eyes, her father and grandfather were right and wrong.
If... If she is only angry about what happened to Giovanna,
then she could leave just like she did seven years ago, only this time bringing Giovanna with her.
However, when she got news of her grandfather's death, when she turned a blind eye to the carwash worker, when she turned her back on her father's orders to help, the only thought on her mind was—
There's no end to it all.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: He showed me how to deal with the famiglie in a comically simple way—

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: He offered them goods they couldn't refuse. Benefits.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: It's not as if the famiglie couldn't take what he had.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But what they always lacked was a great manager. They only knew how to plunder, but never actually learned how to govern.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Relying on his outstanding abilities, he gradually became a celebrity to several prominent famiglie.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And when they fought over who would fill the role of Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici, he became the candidate that everyone was happy with.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Having said all this, I'm sure a lot of you will have questions—

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: You might think Carracci sounds like a guy who played both sides.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But what I'd like to say is, in a country like Siracusa, a country rooted in evil, it has never been possible for a good person to exist.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: To put it mildly, we are all evil.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Should he be saying stuff like that in an inaugural speech?

a.text: October 15th
I met with that judge, Lavinia.
From the way people talk about her, I imagined someone like Carracci, a righteous person who wasn't willing to throw away her integrity.
Meeting her only confirmed that.
There's no way she's unaware of the futility of what she's doing, in our current landscape.
There's no way she's unaware of the fact that should she ever cross any of the famiglia, her life would be in grave danger.
The irony of all this is, the rights of ordinary people that she strives to protect as a judge mean nothing in the eyes of the famiglie.
They mean so little to them that she has not been snuffed out on her path forward.
Talking to her was torture, because I had to hold back my admiration for her and treat her like I would anyone else.
Carracci once joked that my position made him feel at ease because even if he died, he knew I would be there to pick up the torch.
But... what if I also died?
It's not as if I haven't cultivated and won over a number of youths, but they've never had a leader with any real sway like Carracci.
And undoubtedly, Judge Lavinia would make an ideal successor.
Of course, I can't push my ideas on her.
But, I'm afraid I don't have much time left either.
There is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity in front of me. I don't have time to convey each and every one of my thoughts to her.
I do believe, however, that if my plan goes well, Judge Lavinia will at least be willing to look after my daughter.
Alas... Carracci, my old friend, let me put your death to good use.
If our souls can meet once more, I'll have to apologize to you again.
—But, a noble soul like yours probably won't end up in the same place as mine, haha.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ugh, I knew we should've relocated as soon as we could.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But we're just gonna have to work with this, considering everything that happened yesterday.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Gah, that Sankta's a pain in the ass.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: It's just one woman! Surround her!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: My trusty partner here is trying to relax, so mind keeping it down?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ugh, you guys sure love raising hell, don't you?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh, if anyone else was here, they'd probably be like, 'But Exusiai, you also love raising hell too!'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It sure sucks having to do this alone.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What's this? Someone need a helping hand?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I've been wondering, do you, like... have way too much time on your hands?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I'm just like you. We're all waiting for an answer.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What do you mean by that?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Does it make a big difference to you whether or not Texas goes back to Lungmen?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: And as of right now, I want her to go back.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Hmm... Does that mean you're on our side?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Sure does.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Great. Can't party alone.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Sorry, sorry. I shouldn't have said all that depressing stuff.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: However, it should be clear to everyone by now that I'm not here to give an inaugural speech.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I came here to speak from my heart.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Carracci, as bold as his vision was, never mentioned anything to me about his outlook regarding the new city.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The reason for that is, when he took up his position, he was already prepared to die.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: We've all borne witness to what he did over the past two years.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And just when I thought he might make it long enough to see the birth of the new city, he suddenly died a few days ago.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: As for me, that was the last straw.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: So, I cozied up to Famiglia Bellone, recommended myself to them, and obtained this position.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: In that process, I discovered a shocking conspiracy the Bellone and Saluzzo famiglie have been brewing—

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: From the very beginning, they plotted to plunge this city into chaos and seize the newly-built nomadic city.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Then, they will seek to leverage it against Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Don Alberto, this—

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Any news from Bernardo yet?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: No, Don Alberto.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: What's the meaning of this, Bernardo?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Danbrown.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Danbrown!

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: ...I'm here.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You're near Rubio's location, right?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Whack that lunatic.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Yes, Don Alberto.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Alright... I guess I can't keep you out, if you really want to come in.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: You're an idiot.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: What's the point of all this?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: The way you're dressed... Are you an ordinary worker?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I work at a carwash. It's called 'Auto Lavaggio Danbrown.'

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Oh, that rings a bell.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: So, you must be Danbrown then?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: That's me.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Do you have any particular concerns about your job?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Siracusa's gotten soggy and stale. I've had nothing to do, so I found some work for myself.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: That's a shame. You should've looked a little harder.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: You arrogant wise guys think you can lord over us forever.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: You think your only enemies are each other, you never take any of us seriously.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: But, the times are changing. Nothing stays the same forever.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: No matter how nice your words might sound, they're just words.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Can words overthrow the famiglie, or Signora Sicilia?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: No, but I've taken this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and said what I needed to say.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: As for who'll win between the Bellones and Signora Sicilia, I don't know, or care.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: All I know is—this new era has no room for the likes of you.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: If the next chapter of Siracusan history is about to be written, the heroes of that story won't be the famiglie.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: We may have no power. We may indeed be weak.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: But we know that civilization rose to overcome this savagery.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: We pursue a form of equality, an order not rooted in violence.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Violence is in our nature.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Really now? Why, then, are all the famiglie moving in the same direction?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Why are they chasing money and power instead of violence and conflict?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Is killing me today just a cathartic release of this violence?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Or is it because... I got in the way of the people behind you taking power?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: See, you already know the answer.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: And, if you don't mind, I'd like to be the one to finish myself off.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Do you know what this is?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: A gun?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: That's right. I purchased it from Blacksteel a few years ago, through my connections.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: It's hard to use, and it's not very useful against a pack of wise guys lunging at you.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: All it can do is offer a little protection to one as weak as myself.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: By the looks of things, I already figured out who I should be pointing it at years ago.
Rubio slowly raises the gun's muzzle to his temple.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Oh right, Danbrown.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: I hope that one day, you can just be a regular carwash worker here in Siracusa. One who never has to hold a weapon, ever again.

a.text: October 19th
How I yearn to unload everything on my chest in a speech.
But, I cannot.
I have to convince them that I decided to take revenge on the famiglie because of Carracci's death.
Plus, there are some words that cannot be spoken yet.
I'm not here to usher in a new era. I'm not arrogant enough to think that.
I don't even know how many hearts my words will be able to reach.
But, I believe that as long as this country still has people like me, Carracci, and Lavinia...
Then there is still hope for Siracusa.
So, I will write what I wanted to say here:
Having said so much about Carracci, the reality is, as you may realize, I'm not here to talk about Carracci.
I'm here to talk about myself. And all of us, my dear citizens.
We live in a cage called the famiglie.
They may not always directly affect our lives, but they are always a part of it.
Every ordinary person in Siracusa, over the course of their lives, will come to gain their own understanding of the famiglie through various ways.
And eventually, they get used to it.
However, I hope you can take a good look at the people around you, and look back at your own life.
There is one thing we all should understand—
We are human beings. Our lives are very much real. We are not livestock in a pen.
And above all, we are powerful.
Our power comes from the very lives we have created.
The lives the mafiosi relish in were also created by our hands.
This is the country we've built, brick by brick.

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: Judge Lavinia, am I dreaming? Why is my father... talking with a hitman like that?

steps.name: Rubio's Daughter
steps.text: No, father! He's in danger!
Lavinia feels tears welling up in her eyes.
But she does not have time to wipe them, because she already has a premonition in her heart.
She moves to Rubio's daughter and gently covers her ears.
The inhabitants of Volsinii will never forget this day.
On a clear morning, the crisp clarion call of a pistol's muzzle reverberates across Volsinii through every radio.
Former Volsinii Segretario di Sicurezza Alimentare Rubio died during his inaugural speech, taking over as Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici.
The chaos that ensued, though it would be subdued before half a day's time, in fact became the first step toward a new era for Siracusa.
